cards.term: What is the role of a local controller?
cards.definition: Provide service to and from the terminal environment while maintain appropriate separation requirements.

cards.term: What is the phraseology to issue a takeoff clearance?
cards.definition:
(Callsign), Runway [Runway], cleared for takeoff.

Ex: AAL123, Runway 8R, cleared for takeoff.

cards.term: What is the phraseology to issue line up and wait?
cards.definition:
(Callsign), Runway [Runway], line up and wait.

Ex: AAL123, Runway 8R, line up and wait.

cards.term: Is the issuance of the wind required in a takeoff clearance?
cards.definition: No, unless there is a tailwind on the departing runway.

cards.term: Based on the following wind, what operation would KFLL be in? 06016
cards.definition: East operations (landing and departing 10L/10R)

cards.term: Based on the following wind, what operation would KTPA be in? 160008
cards.definition: South operations (landing and departing 19L/19R)

cards.term:
Based on the following wind what operation would KFLL be in?

010019G23
cards.definition: East operations (landing and departing 10L/10R)

cards.term: What does winds calm mean?
cards.definition:
Wind is calm when less than 3 knots

7110.65 2-6-3 (b)

cards.term: What is a radar departure?
cards.definition: A departure going into the radar environment (going to be talking with the departure controller)

cards.term: What is the standard terminal radar separation?
cards.definition: 3nm

cards.term: By how many degrees must two aircraft's departure courses diverge by to reduce the separation 3nm to 1nm?
cards.definition:
15 degrees. 

Note: 10 degrees if both aircraft are on an RNAV SID

cards.term: If an aircraft is holding short of the runway on your frequency from ground control and you notice the aircraft is not in compliance with an SOP altitude. Is it your responsibility to amend the aircrafts flight plan before issuing a takeoff clearance?
cards.definition: Yes

cards.term: What is required to use runway 10/28 at KTPA?
cards.definition: Local control must coordinate with the affected TRACON sectors.

cards.term: What is an ATIS?
cards.definition: Automated Terminal Information System. A recorded message which tells pilots about the current conditions of the airport such as wx, and notams.

cards.term: What is required in an ATIS?
cards.definition:
- Airport/facility name.
- Phonetic letter code.
- Time of the latest weather sequence (UTC).
- Weather information consisting of:
- Wind direction and velocity.
- Visibility.
- Obstructions to vision.
- Present weather consisting of: sky condition, temperature, dew point, altimeter, a density altitude advisory when appropriate, and other pertinent remarks included in the official weather observation. Always include weather observation remarks of lightning, cumulonimbus, and towering cumulus clouds.

cards.term: How often must an ATIS be updated?
cards.definition: Hourly

cards.term: What must you issue to a VFR inbound (coming directly into your airspace at FLL- hasn't talked to approach) apart from patten entry and runway assignment?
cards.definition:
The local altimeter

Ex: N123AB, Fort Lauderdale Tower, enter left downwind runway 10L, Fort Lauderdale altimeter 30.13

cards.term: True or false: visual separation waves all other forms of separation
cards.definition: True

cards.term: What is tower-applied visual separation?
cards.definition:
The tower controller sees the aircraft involved and issues instruction as necessary to ensure that aircraft avoid each other.

Note: Tower does not need to inform the aircraft that tower-applied visual separation is being used

cards.term: What is pilot applied visual separation?
cards.definition:
Pilot-applied visual separation is an Air Traffic Control (ATC) procedure where a pilot, upon seeing another aircraft, assumes responsibility for maintaining safe spacing from it.

Make sure to tell the other aircraft involved that "(Traffic) has you in sight and will maintain visual separation"

cards.term: What is the IFR-VFR separation standard in Class C airspace?
cards.definition:
- Target Resolution
- 500 ft. vertical
- Visual separation

cards.term: What are the separation standards in Class B?
cards.definition:
1. Standard IFR services to IFR aircraft.
2. VFR aircraft must be separated from VFR/IFR aircraft that weigh more than 19,000 pounds and turbojets by no less than:
 - 1.5 miles separation or
 - 500 ft vertical separation or
 - visual separation
3. VFR aircraft must be separated from all VFR/IFR aircraft which weigh 19,000 pounds or less by a minimum of:
 - Target resolution or
 - 500 ft vertical or
 - visual separation

cards.term: What form of separation are VFR aircraft guaranteed in class D airspace?
cards.definition: Runway separation

cards.term: What is a CTRD/TDW
cards.definition: Certified Tower Radar Display/Tower Display Workstation

cards.term: How are you authorized to use your TDW at FLL?
cards.definition:
LC shall retain STARS data blocks to maintain continuous aircraft identity for aircraft that will remain within LC's delegated airspace, including the traffic pattern.

Reference 3-5 of the FLL SOP for more information

cards.term: How are you authorized to use your TDW at TPA?
cards.definition:
LC shall provide radar services to VFR aircraft only when the aircraft's entry into and/or exit from Tampa Class B airspace occurs within LC's delegated airspace. C. LC shall retain STARS data blocks to maintain continuous aircraft identity for aircraft that will remain within LC's delegated airspace, including the traffic pattern.

Reference 3-6 of the TPA SOP for more information

cards.term: What segment of the VFR traffic pattern is N535PT depicted?
cards.definition: Downwind

cards.term: What segment of the VFR traffic pattern is N535PT depicted?
cards.definition: Base

cards.term: What segment of the VFR traffic pattern is N535PT depicted?
cards.definition: Crosswind

cards.term: What segment of the VFR traffic pattern is N535PT depicted?
cards.definition: Final

cards.term: What segment of the VFR traffic pattern is N535PT depicted?
cards.definition: Departure leg

cards.term: Which legs of the traffic pattern can be extended?
cards.definition: Upwind, crosswind, downwind

cards.term: What does "cleared for the option" indicate?
cards.definition: The plane can preform: full stop, touch and go, low approach, stop and go, or missed approach.

cards.term: How would you tell a plane that you want to clear them for the option, but you do not want them to preform a stop and go?
cards.definition: "N123AB, wind 120 @ 5, runway 10L cleared for the option, unable stop and go"

cards.term: How would you restrict an aircraft to only preform a touch and go?
cards.definition: "N123AB, wind 120 @ 7 runway 10L cleared touch and go"

cards.term: what is the standard traffic pattern direction?
cards.definition: Left closed traffic

cards.term: Is an A300 considered a heavy aircraft?
cards.definition: Yes

cards.term: Is a B757-200 considered a heavy
cards.definition: No

cards.term: Is a B757-300 considered a heavy
cards.definition: No

cards.term: What is the heavy jet wake turbulence separation time (minutes)?
What is the super jet wake turbulence separation time (minutes)?
What is the CWT (consolidated wake turbulence) separation minimum for C behind B
What is the CWT separation minimum for E behind B
What is the preferred way to apply wake turbulence separation? Time or mileage?
cards.definition: Mileage

cards.term: When can you use mileage instead of time for wake turbulence separation?
cards.definition:
1. aircraft taking off from the same runway or a parallel runway separated by less than 2,500 feet
2. Separate a Category I aircraft behind a Category E aircraft by 2 minutes when departing:
 - The same runway or a parallel runway separated by less than 700 feet.
 - A parallel runway separated by 700 feet or more if projected flight paths will cross.
3. Separate aircraft departing from a parallel runway separated by 2,500 feet or more if projected flight paths will cross

7110.65 3-9-6

cards.term: What is a departure release?
cards.definition: An authorization from the overlying controller to let you (local) give a takeoff clearance.

cards.term: What is a rolling call?
cards.definition: Coordination initiated by local to the overlying controller that assists the overlying controller in radar identifying the departure aircraft.

cards.term: When is a departure release/rolling call required at FLL?
cards.definition:
- Non-turbojet departures to the south.
- Turbojet and non-turbojet departures destined for airports south of FLL within Miami Approach airspace.

cards.term: What is the coordination list?
cards.definition: The Coordination List, also referred to as the "Rundown List," shows coordination message information for departing flights prior to their radar track association. Flights are removed from coordination lists upon their acquisition by radar. A coordination list provides a means where a tower controller typically can convey the sequence and related data of pending departures to the sector controller (also called the departure controller) who will be handling the flight.

cards.term: What would be the minimum separation needed for 2 A320 aircraft both on the FRSBE SID?
cards.definition: 3nm airborne

cards.term: What does SRS stand for?
cards.definition: Same runway separation

cards.term: What is a CAT 1 aircraft?
cards.definition: Typically, small piston driven aircraft (ex. C172)

cards.term: What is a CAT 2 aircraft?
cards.definition: Typically, medium sized twin aircraft (ex. B350)

cards.term: What is a CAT 3 aircraft?
cards.definition: Typically, large jet engine aircraft (ex. A320)

cards.term: What is the SRS of a CAT 1 aircraft behind a CAT 2 aircraft?
cards.definition: 3,000ft and airborne

cards.term: What is the SRS of a CAT 1 aircraft behind a CAT 1 aircraft?
cards.definition: 3,000ft and airborne

cards.term: What is the SRS of a CAT2 aircraft behind a CAT 1 aircraft?
cards.definition: 4,500ft and airborne

cards.term: What is the SRS of a CAT3 aircraft behind a CAT 2 aircraft?
cards.definition: 6,000ft and airborne

cards.term: What is the SRS of a CAT3 aircraft behind a CAT 3 aircraft?
cards.definition: 6,000ft and airborne

cards.term: What is the SRS of a CAT3 aircraft behind a CAT 1 aircraft?
cards.definition: 6,000ft and airborne

cards.term: What is the SRS of a CAT 1 aircraft behind a CAT 3 aircraft?
cards.definition: 6,000ft and airborne

cards.term: Anytime a CAT 3 aircraft is involved, SRS is always _____ft?
cards.definition: 6,000ft and airborne

cards.term: Does SRS take priority over wake turbulence in terms of when you can depart a plane?
cards.definition: No. Wake turbulence separation is prioritized over SRS.

cards.term: Can you tell an aircraft to LUAW (line up and wait) at KRSW when you have already cleared an aircraft to land on that runway?
cards.definition: No

cards.term: Can you tell an aircraft to LUAW at KFLL when you have already cleared an aircraft to land on that runway?
cards.definition: Yes

cards.term: When are you permitted to utilize line up and wait?
cards.definition: Anytime at airports with an ASDE-X and only when you have not cleared an aircraft to land at a non ASDE-X airport.

cards.term: What is an intersection departure?
cards.definition: When you depart an aircraft at an intersection of a runway. For example, runway 10L at B4.

cards.term: How do you issue a takeoff clearance at the intersection B4 of 10L at KFLL?
cards.definition: "N123AB, runway 10L at B4 cleared for takeoff"

cards.term: What is the proper phraseology to cancel a takeoff clearance?
cards.definition: "N123AB, cancel takeoff clearance"

cards.term: What is an overhead maneuver?
cards.definition: A series of predetermined turns that aircraft perform to enter a Visual Flight Rules (VFR) traffic pattern and land. 7110.65 3-10-12

cards.term: At what point during the overhead maneuver does the aircraft's IFR flight plan terminate?
cards.definition: Initial point 7110.65 3-10-12

cards.term: What is the phraseology to issue an overhead maneuver?
cards.definition:
"N123AB, runway 10L wind 150 @ 10, pattern altitude one thousand, report initial" "N123AB, break at midfield, report break" "N123AB, cleared to land"

OR 

"N123AB, runway 10L wind 150 @ 10, left turns, report initial" "N123AB, report break" "N123AB, cleared to land"

Note: either or both pattern altitude and direction may be omitted if standard (standard altitude 1000, standard direction left)

cards.term: What does LAHSO mean?
cards.definition: Land and Hold Short Operations

cards.term: What are the conditions that need to be met in order to utilize LAHSO?
cards.definition:
The below LAHSO operations are authorized in VMC only, between sunrise and sunset, provided that the LAHSO runway is dry, and has a tailwind component of less than 3 knots. 

Reference specific SOPs for size requirements

cards.term: What is the phraseology to issue a LAHSO landing clearance for runway 28 at KTPA?
cards.definition: "N123AB, Tampa Tower, wind 270 @ 19, runway 28 cleared to land, hold short runway 1R"

cards.term: Can LAHSO be used in this case?
cards.definition: Yes

cards.term: What is a safety logic system?
cards.definition: A safety logic system is implemented at KMIA and KFLL and provides auditory and visual warnings when there is the possibility for multiple aircraft to be operating on the same runway. This is especially helpful in low visibility situations when the TWR CAB display is unusable.

cards.term: What is the VFR transition that goes overtop of the KFLL airport?
cards.definition: Fort Lauderdale overhead transition. (review skyvector - MIA TAC/FLY chart)

cards.term: What transition does the Fort Lauderdale overhead transition connect to?
cards.definition: Red road transition

cards.term: What would the phraseology be to instruct someone to join the Fort Lauderdale overhead transition southbound at 2,500ft?,
cards.definition: "N123AB, join the Fort Lauderdale overhead transition southbound at 2,500ft"

cards.term: What transition goes overtop the Tampa airport?
cards.definition: Bridge transition

cards.term: What altitude should the bridge transition aircraft be assigned?
cards.definition: westbound IFR at 4000 or VFR at 3500, and eastbound IFR at 3000 or VFR at 2500

cards.term: In the event of a go around, what are the general procedures a TWR controller should follow (non SOP specific)?
cards.definition:
Provide control instructions to the aircraft (fly heading 090, climb and maintain 3,000ft) 

Coordinate with the appropriate TRACON controller (typically departure)

cards.term: What are 3 techniques that can be used to help sequence VFR pattern work aircraft?
cards.definition: 360 turns, 270 turn to base, or S-turns

cards.term: Are TWR controllers required to accept VFR pattern work aircraft?
cards.definition: No

cards.term: If a VFR aircraft calls EYW TWR and requests to make a full stop landing, and EYW TWR responds with "Aircraft calling, standby", can the aircraft proceed into the delta airspace?
cards.definition: No. 2 way radio communication has not been established.

cards.term: A B737 calls TPA TWR 7 miles out on the visual approach 1R. TPA TWR has a 2 VFR aircraft in a right pattern for 1R currently. Assuming no other traffic in the area or on final, what could TPA TWR do with the B737 to prevent having to sequence the pattern work aircraft around the B737?
cards.definition: Side step the B737 to runway 1L.

cards.term: What is the side step phraseology?
cards.definition: N123AB, change to runway 1L, wind 010 @ 15 runway 1L cleared to land.

cards.term: A B787 is on a 2 mile final and a B737 is on a 7 mile final for the same runway (1L). The B787 is already cleared to land. The B737 calls TWR with the following call: "Tampa Tower, N123AB ILS 1L". What should the response be assuming so other aircraft are in the area?
cards.definition: N123AB, Tampa Tower, number 2 following a B787 on a 2 mile final, caution wake turbulence, wind 010 @ 9 , runway 1L cleared to land. 7110.65 3-10-3

cards.term: Is landing sequence (e.g."Number 2") required to be issued to an aircraft in a landing clearance?
cards.definition: No, issuing the landing sequence to an aircraft is optional at airports where arrivals are sequenced in by an approach controller.
